problem:
Describe the set $S={...,3,6,9,12,15,...}$ using a constructive definition.

*Hint: Take ${a}_{1}=3$ in the sequence that generates the elements of $S.$*

$$
n+2
$$
worked_solution:
Notice that the elements of our set

$$
…,\,3,\,6,\,9,\,12,\,15,\,…
$$

form a two-way infinite arithmetic sequence with common difference $d=3:$

$$
\begin{aligned}d & =3 \\  & =6-3 \\  & =9-6 \\  & =12-9 \\  & =⋯\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, setting  ${a}_{1}=3,$ the $n$th term ${a}_{n}$ of our sequence for $n\in Z$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n} & ={a}_{1}+(n-1)\cdot d \\  & =3+(n-1)\cdot 3 \\  & =3+3n-3 \\  & =3n.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can define our set using a constructive definition as follows:

$$
S={3n\,:\,n\in Z}
$$
